subject: Social Habits
title: Being brave and trying
objectives: Children will try a new activity with encouragement.
Children will say "I can try" and keep going for a short time.
content: Trying something new, saying "I can try", and keeping going.
teachingActivities: Praise effort rather than result ("You kept trying"); offer a small first step; stay beside a hesitant child; never compare children; let children refuse and return; model trying and making mistakes yourself.
learnerActivities: Try a new activity with encouragement, say "I can try" and keep going for a short time.
resources: A balance beam on the floor
A puppet who is afraid and then tries
assessment: Observe whether each child tries a new activity with encouragement and says "I can try".
expectedOutcomes: Tries a new activity with encouragement.
Says "I can try" with a prompt.

lessons.title: Trying something new
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will try a new activity with encouragement.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt manners, kindness, honesty, helping and respect over two terms.
lessons.starter: Show a puppet looking at a tower of cups and say "I have never done this. I will try."
teacherActivities: Show how to stack two cups and say "I tried."
Invite each child to try stacking one cup.
Praise the trying, not only the tower.
Give the brave badge to the puppet and say "Brave to try."
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to stack two cups and say "I tried." Children: Children watch and clap.
Step 2. Teacher: Invite each child to try stacking one cup. Children: Child tries stacking a cup.
Step 3. Teacher: Praise the trying, not only the tower. Children: Child smiles and tries again.
Step 4. Teacher: Give the brave badge to the puppet and say "Brave to try." Children: Children cheer for the puppet.

practical.title: Stack and try
practical.safety: Use large light plastic cups only and keep children seated. Never force a child to try; stay close and offer a first step.

differentiation.support: Stack the first cup together and let the child add one.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to try stacking four cups.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Tries a new activity with encouragement
lessons.homeConnection: Praise your child for trying new things, not only for succeeding.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "try a new activity with encouragement" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: I can try, I can try, I can try again.

lessons.title: I can try
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will say "I can try" before an activity.
successCriteria: Says I can try with a prompt
Starts a task after saying it
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt manners, kindness, honesty, helping and respect over two terms.
lessons.starter: Say "When something looks hard, we say: I can try."
teacherActivities: Model saying "I can try" before a puzzle.
Let each child say it before a task.
Notice effort and say "You are trying."
learnerActivities: Child says I can try and begins.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Model saying "I can try" before a puzzle. Children: Children repeat I can try.
Step 2. Teacher: Let each child say it before a task. Children: Child says I can try and begins.
Step 3. Teacher: Notice effort and say "You are trying." Children: Child continues with the task.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "Well done for trying." Children: Children smile.

practical.title: I can try tasks
practical.safety: Choose tasks that children can mostly do and use large pieces. Never say a task is easy or hard.

differentiation.support: Say the words together and start together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say it to a friend before they start.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do you say before you try?

expectedOutcomes: Says I can try with a prompt
Starts a task after saying it
lessons.conclusion: Say "I can try" together and clap.
lessons.homeConnection: Teach your child to say "I can try" before new tasks.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "say "I can try" before an activity" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Keeping going
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will keep going with a task for a short time when it is not easy.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt manners, kindness, honesty, helping and respect over two terms.
lessons.starter: Build a tower that falls and say "Oops. Let us try again."
teacherActivities: Show a tower that falls and rebuild it.
Say "If it is hard, I can ask for help."
Let children build or do a puzzle.
Praise the trying with specific words.
learnerActivities: Children watch and say try again.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show a tower that falls and rebuild it. Children: Children watch and say try again.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "If it is hard, I can ask for help." Children: Children repeat ask for help.
Step 3. Teacher: Let children build or do a puzzle. Children: Child tries and tries again.
Step 4. Teacher: Praise the trying with specific words. Children: Child smiles and nods.

practical.title: Try again
steps: Ask for help if you need it.
practical.safety: Use large light blocks and keep a safe distance from falling towers. Step in only when a child asks for help.

differentiation.extension: Ask the child to help a friend who is stuck.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we do if it falls?

lessons.conclusion: Look at the finished work and say "You kept trying."
lessons.homeConnection: Let your child try again before you help.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "keep going with a task for a short time when it is not easy" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Brave steps
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will try a physical challenge with a friendly adult beside them.
successCriteria: Tries to walk along a line or beam
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt manners, kindness, honesty, helping and respect over two terms.
resources: A line of tape or a low beam on the floor
lessons.starter: Show a line on the floor and say "Can you walk on the line? Let us try."
teacherActivities: Show how to walk along the line with arms out.
Hold hands and walk the line with each child.
Let children try with less help.
Say "I did it" and give a badge.
learnerActivities: Child tries to walk the line.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to walk along the line with arms out. Children: Children watch.
Step 2. Teacher: Hold hands and walk the line with each child. Children: Child tries to walk the line.
Step 3. Teacher: Let children try with less help. Children: Child walks with less support.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "I did it" and give a badge. Children: Child says I did it.

practical.title: Walk the line
practical.safety: Use tape on the floor or a very low beam with soft mats beside it. Stay close and keep a second adult watching.

differentiation.support: Hold the child’s hand all the way along.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to walk backwards or carry a bean bag.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Give a badge and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Let your child try a safe challenge and praise the effort.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "try a physical challenge with a friendly adult beside them" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 1 trying check
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child tries new things and keeps going.
successCriteria: Says I can try with a prompt
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt manners, kindness, honesty, helping and respect over two terms.
lessons.starter: Sing the try song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: cups, puzzle and line.
At each station watch how the child tries.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: cups, puzzle and line. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station watch how the child tries. Children: Child tries with a prompt.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Trying stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station closely and keep floors clear. Use large light items only.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use one station.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to encourage a friend.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: tries a new activity; says I can try; keeps going after a mistake; asks for help.

questions.question: What do you do if it falls?

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 1
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child tries new things and keeps going" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
